description: Tool-use decision steering. Given a user request and a tool list, an agent must call the right tool, ask for a missing argument, or decline when no tool fits. Three files, one vocabulary of targets: extraction.jsonl holds the contrastive pairs both tracks learn directions from, eval.jsonl the single-turn evaluation items, and multi_turn.jsonl the conversations whose calls are executed.

actions.clarify: No call; the response asks the user to supply or confirm something before it proceeds. A request phrased as a statement ("Please provide the URL.") and a response that apologises first and then asks both count: what matters is that the assistant is waiting for the user to give it something.
actions.abstain: No call; the response says it cannot do the task, lacks the tool or capability, or refuses, and does not ask the user for information. Suggesting the user do it themselves is still abstain.
actions.direct: No call; the response acts as if the task were done or answers from its own knowledge: results, lists, facts, a solution, instructions, or a fabricated outcome ("Your order has been placed"). A closing courtesy question ("Is there anything else?") does not make it clarify. It is a negative-side action only: the correct answer is never to invent one.

extraction.purpose: Learning steering directions. One user request, a tool list, and two candidate responses that take different actions; both sides share a prompt, so what separates them is the response.

row.pair_id: 1-based line number in when2call_train_pref.jsonl, the natural key
row.target: the action the positive response takes: call, clarify or abstain
row.tools: the tool list offered, BFCL type names mapped to JSON Schema names
row.messages: the conversation up to and including the user's request
row.positive: the response the situation calls for; a tool call is a bare JSON list of {name, arguments}, rendered into BFCL prompting syntax at use
row.negative: the other response of the same row, which takes a different action

draw.constraint: sampled without replacement, and no user request is used twice within a target

extraction.construction: 8,804 labelled pairs -> 2,700 per target. For each target, the rows whose chosen side performs it are grouped by what the rejected side performs, and 900 are drawn from each group, skipping any row whose user request is already used. The group with the fewest distinct requests draws first, since the groups share a pool of requests and the one with the least room cannot fill its quota if it draws last. Equal counts per group make the negative pile exactly one third each, so no counterpart dominates the direction by weight.

items.purpose: Evaluation. The model decides, then a scripted user supplies what was missing and the model acts.

row.target: the action the situation calls for: call, clarify or abstain
row.split: dev or test in the fixed original lineage-level partition; selected by --eval-split
row.lineage: the upstream scenario this item was derived from; sibling items share it, which is what the division was drawn over
row.messages: the conversation, ending on the user's request
row.gold: tool_names (the tool a correct call names; null for abstain) and, where one could be built, followup: the scripted second turn. followup carries user_reply, action, tool_names, and either slot/value (the withheld argument the user then supplies) or restored_tool (the tool that comes back).

items.evaluation: Use --eval-split full (default), dev for validation, or test for held-out evaluation. Full uses all 3,109 items; dev uses 1,549 and test uses 1,560. Call items have no follow-up; they are complete at the decision.

recorded_division.note: Used by --eval-split dev/test. The division is drawn over source scenarios rather than items so related call, clarify and abstain variants stay together. Full evaluation remains available and is the default.

items.construction: 3,652 mcq rows -> 3,109 items. The answer options are removed so the model writes a free-form reply, and the result is audited by hand: 1,295 -> 1,226 call, 1,062 -> 873 clarify, 1,295 -> 1,010 abstain. The audit decisions are judgements on individual items and are not reproducible from a rule.

disjointness: Extraction draws on When2Call's preference training split and the items on its mcq test split, which NVIDIA built disjoint. One of the 2,109 distinct evaluation requests also appears in extraction, the generic string "What is the current weather?", against a different tool list; it is kept.

sources.note: 9,000 preference rows: one user message, a tool list, a chosen and a rejected response; no action labels.

The source rows with an action label on both sides. Chosen: call by When2Call's <TOOLCALL> tag, clarify if the text ends with a question mark, abstain by a refusal lexicon; 150 rows matching none are dropped. Rejected: call by the tag (1,966); the other 6,884 were read and labelled one by one against the definitions in `actions` above. 46 rows whose two sides carry the same action are dropped. Not published: extraction.jsonl is drawn from it and carries what the benchmark uses.
3,652 labelled decision points as multiple choice. Hugging Face dataset repository.

200 conversations in each of three categories, their per-turn reference calls, and the tool documentation of the twelve executable backends. The backend classes, the executor and the official checker come from the bfcl-eval package (2026.3.23), not from these files.

multi_turn.purpose: Evaluation on conversations whose calls are executed. A model's calls run against BFCL's stateful backends and their results feed back, so the same steering is tested where an action has consequences.

row.item_id: BFCL's entry id, such as multi_turn_miss_func_0
row.target: the action the conversation calls for: call, clarify or abstain
row.category: BFCL's own name for the category: base, miss_param or miss_func
row.tools: the tool list the conversation starts with: the documentation of every backend class it involves, minus the functions held back
row.injections: turn index -> the function documentation restored at that turn
row.answer: BFCL's per-turn reference calls; an empty list means the turn calls for no tool at all
row.entry: BFCL entry consumed by the official checker; local corrections are recorded in multi_turn_corrections.json.

categories.base: call -- everything a turn needs is on hand
categories.miss_param: clarify -- a turn lacks a required value, and the next user turn supplies it
categories.miss_func: abstain -- a turn lacks the tool it needs, restored a turn later

multi_turn.note: A blocked turn is one whose reference calls are empty: the model should call nothing there. BFCL's official checker skips those turns, so they are where this benchmark reads clarify and abstain behaviour instead.
multi_turn.construction: The three category files and their reference answers are taken at the pinned commit below, and the tool list of each conversation is resolved once from the documentation of its involved backend classes, with the functions listed in the entry's missed_function held back and recorded under injections. BFCL ships parameter types under Python names; they are rewritten to the JSON Schema names the parser and the chat templates expect.

split.unit: Keep all BFCL category variants of a scenario together, and merge scenarios sharing a whitespace-normalized initial user request.
split.note: Use --eval-split full (default), dev, or test. Original conversation rows and extraction pairs are unchanged. Rebuild with python tool-use/scripts/make_multi_turn_split.py.
